Meta just open sourced Muse Gadgets, a hacker-focused SDK for building custom hardware displays and controllers using ESP32 boards and Raspberry Pis paired with the Muse mobile app. 🔌✨

Building connected IoT hardware usually means spending weeks writing custom companion mobile apps just to handle pairing, security, and control. 

The Muse Gadget SDK solves this by bridging your custom workbench hardware—displays, buttons, sensors, and actuators—directly with iOS and Android companion apps via secure token pairing. 🚀

Key Features to Hack On:
• ESP32 Device SDK: Support for custom screens, audio I/O, and sensor integration on standard microcontrollers.
• Linux Device SDK: Turn spare Raspberry Pis or Linux boxes into programmable home automation or sysadmin gadgets.
• Seamless Mobile Pairing: Use the official iOS and Android apps with a dedicated developer mode for discovering devices.
• AI Coding Agent Support: Includes AGENTS.md configurations optimized for coding agents like Muse Code.

Whether you want to build a custom desktop monitoring dashboard using an ESP32 or set up a Raspberry Pi gadget for home automation, this gives you a production-ready starting point without building the mobile stack from scratch. 🛠️

Check out the repo and start building your next connected gadget today:
https://github.com/facebookincubator/muse-gadget-sdk

Stop wasting tokens and time on LLM-generated HTML walls of text by letting AI agents output lightweight markdown that instantly compiles into gorgeous single-page explainers. 📉💸

We’ve all been there: asking an LLM for code documentation or architecture maps, only to watch it burn through thousands of tokens writing raw CSS, endless wrapper divs, and messy SVG coordinates. 

QingYunA/answer-me-with-html fixes this completely. 

Instead of forcing models to write full HTML, this tool lets AI agents output concise, token-efficient markdown. A bundled CLI tool then transforms that content into a structured, readable, single-page HTML explainer in milliseconds, slashing your output token usage by over 7x. 🚀

Key Features:
• Token-Efficient Generation: Models write roughly 7x fewer tokens by focusing purely on content and structure instead of boilerplate styling.
• Automated Explainer Players: Converts drafted narrative beats into self-contained, 3Blue1Brown-style interactive video players with synchronized system or ElevenLabs voice narration.
• Always-On Contextual Mode: Automatically triggers lightweight multi-panel explanatory pages whenever an agent delivers conclusions, summaries, or architectural comparisons.
• Seamless Multi-Agent Integration: Ships smoothly as a native skill compatible with developer tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode.

Whether you are mapping unfamiliar module dependencies, generating interactive technical onboarding guides, or comparing architectural trade-offs on the fly, this saves serious waiting time and cognitive load. Get immediate, beautifully styled visual artifacts like sequence diagrams, state diagrams, and comparison tables that you can easily review offline. 📊✨

Check it out on GitHub and star the project to support the build:
https://github.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html

Tired of spending hours decoding dense academic papers and fighting with broken formatting? 

EasyRead bridges the language and cognitive gap for researchers tackling dense technical literature by combining local PDF processing, AI translation, and interactive querying in an Electron wrapper. 

If you are an AI researcher, ML engineer, or grad student constantly buried in arXiv preprints, this localized reading assistant automates translation, formatting, and interactive querying of complex academic PDFs while keeping your data private.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your literature reviews:
- Native rendering of text and mathematical formulas via KaTeX and three-line tables.
- Dual-pane reading interface with paragraph-level alignment and real-time page highlight sync.
- Multi-engine AI support including DeepSeek, Ollama, Claude Code, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- Context-aware AI chat and CLI integration to query highlighted sections and export annotations as Markdown or offline HTML.
- 100% local library management backed by JSON files and local storage with no external database required.

Speed up your reading workflow and process sensitive research papers entirely offline. 

Check out the repo and drop a star if it helps your research:
https://github.com/Edwardxlai/easyread

What happens when you fuse Modern Warfare 2, Skate 3, and Minecraft into a single, high-performance custom game engine built entirely in Rust? 

Systems engineers and game devs, check this out. chasmlol/2010-rust-rewrite-mashup is an eccentric, high-performance systems engineering showcase built on top of IW4L, a from-scratch Rust rewrite of Modern Warfare 2. 

Building complex, cross-genre engines usually means wrestling with massive technical debt, memory safety issues, and garbage collection overhead. This project solves that by proving the sheer performance headroom, safety, and expressiveness of Rust when handling real-time physics integration, memory extraction, and reverse-engineered binary interaction.

Notable Features:
- Cross-Engine Asset and Mechanics Integration: Combines MW2 multiplayer gunplay, HUD, and damage models with an endless procedural Minecraft world engine complete with reactive mobs and destructible terrain.
- Engine-Level Physics Interoperability: Seamlessly injects Skate 3 board physics and trick systems directly into maps via custom input handling, letting you skate across tactical or voxel landscapes.
- Autonomous Asset Sourcing: Automatically fetches vanilla Minecraft client assets straight from official Mojang servers on first boot to remain copyright-compliant while delivering an out-of-the-box playable experience.
- Comprehensive Input and Controller Mapping: Delivers native console button layouts, fully rebindable KBM controls, and accurate console-style aim assist in a non-official engine.

Whether you want to study low-level engine architecture, experiment with runtime asset ingestion pipelines, or just marvel at what Rust can do, this repository is a masterclass.

Explore the source code and dive into the architecture here:
https://github.com/chasmlol/2010-rust-rewrite-mashup
